rationale: The product is indexed by i over J, so its factor must be alpha_i; alpha_j leaves j free and does not describe the stated family product.
The preceding factors and intersection are indexed by j; the printed product binds i while leaving j free.
The proof fixed E_1 through E_n and no k is bound in this implication; the arbitrariness claim must refer to those n sets.
The factor is parameterized by j through both i_j and F_j; binding i leaves j free.
The proposition declares the family h_i, so the generated sigma-algebra and measurability argument must use h_i(X_i), not an unbound common h. Both occurrences carry the same repair.
The proof declared E_j in Sigma_{i_j}; E_{i_j} is not declared and must be E_j in the diagonal-preimage identity.
The same declared events E_j must appear in the measure-product computation; E_{i_j} is undefined in this proof.
In the product-space cylinder argument E_i must equal the full factor space Omega_i outside finite J; X_i denotes a random variable and cannot serve as the factor set.
F_{ij} are the declared Borel target sets; E_i is the product-coordinate event and E_{ij} is nowhere defined.

The H_i are coordinate subsets whose product lies in the product space; J is undefined, and membership in Sigma_i concerns each coordinate map phi_i. The printed intersection and unindexed preimage are ill-typed.
The proof defined the tail event E_a and immediately uses its measure; bare E is not defined in this argument.
The theorem quantifies E_r for r up to n and its displayed product also runs to n; j_r leaves the family length inconsistent.
The proof repeats the theorem's n-member family and uses r only as the running index; the terminal subscript must be n.
The proof declared nu_{X_1} as the distribution of X_1; mu_{X_1} is not defined in this section.
The Taylor argument defines the function h in the immediately preceding sentence; no h_i function is declared there.
The subsequent factorization subtracts b a_i and b c for every i. The printed expression leaves i free outside the sum and subtracts c only once syntactically.
Here Z sums X_n inclusively from n=0 through Y, so E(Z)=gamma sum_{n>=0}P(Y>=n)=gamma(E(Y)+1). The unshifted Wald form applies to a one-indexed or exclusive convention.
The endnote summarizes the Taylor estimate proved above, whose linear term is b a_i; omitting b contradicts both h'(0)=a_i and the preceding displayed bound.
